title: Redstone: Byte listens and switches on
reflection: Where in real life do you find an input and an output like Byte's levers and lamp? Think of a device that needs two things at once (AND) to work.

steps.goal: MINE has put a redstone lamp behind your Byte, an iron door in front of it and a lever on each side. Write a program that switches on the lamp behind Byte.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: when your program ends, the lamp behind Byte must be on.
hints: redstone.setOutput(side, true) sends a redstone signal from one side of Byte: "back", "front", "left", "right", "top", "bottom".
The lamp is behind Byte: redstone.setOutput("back", true).
block_hints: In the Redstone group, "redstone signal [side] set to true" sends a signal from one side of Byte.
The lamp is behind Byte: "redstone signal behind set to true".

steps.goal: Make the door follow the left lever: open when the lever is on, closed when it's off. When your program is listening, MINE pulls the lever a few times to test it.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: the door must open when the left lever is on and close when it's off, every time.
hints: redstone.getInput("left") is true when the left lever is on. Send the same value to the door, in front: redstone.setOutput("front", ...).
Repeat forever: while true do ... os.pullEvent("redstone") end. os.pullEvent("redstone") waits until a redstone signal changes.
block_hints: "signal from left?" is true when the left lever is on. Put it in "redstone signal in front set to ...", for the door.
Repeat forever: "repeat while true", and at the end of it "wait for a redstone change".

steps.goal: Now both levers: the lamp behind Byte must be on only when the left lever AND the right lever are on. MINE will try all four ways.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: the lamp must be on only when both levers are on.
hints: a and b is true only when a and b are both true: redstone.getInput("left") and redstone.getInput("right").
Inside while true do ... end: send that value to the lamp, behind, then wait with os.pullEvent("redstone").
block_hints: In Logic, the "and" block is true only when both sides are true: "signal from left?" and "signal from right?".
Inside "repeat while true": "redstone signal behind set to" with that block, then "wait for a redstone change".
